spans.text: Curated file collections to hand to Claude Design for generating UIs that expose [&] Protocol backend functionality through the web.
Why bundles and not the whole repo
. Feeding the whole 100k-file monorepo dilutes the signal. Each bundle below is ~10-20 files, covers one scope, and includes cover notes explaining intent.
Single React/Vite SPA that exposes every product's MCP surface under one nav, one auth, one theme
SvelteKit canvas UI rendering Graphonomous + body-* traces as a navigable 3D space
Protocol spec, nav component, palette — referenced by both bundles
Upload to Claude Design as the project context

is included in both bundles. Unzip twice and dedupe if that's wasteful.

is already started (React SPA, Supabase auth). Its master spec calls for it to be the meta-platform aggregating every product. Today it's a shell — Claude Design should flesh out the dashboards that expose FleetPrompt / Agentelic / SpecPrompt / Graphonomous / Delegatic / PRISM / body-* MCP tools as first-class web pages.
is specced as the spatial-cognition visualization layer. Its mission is to make Graphonomous memory graphs + body-* traces
. A 3D-ish SvelteKit SPA is the natural form.
Both are greenfield enough that Claude Design has room to design, but grounded by existing specs (1087 + 131 lines respectively) so it won't invent products.
Per-product Studio UIs (Agentelic Studio, SpecPrompt editor, FleetPrompt publisher) — these should ship as
rather than separate deployments. Keeping only two UI buildouts keeps the operator nav singular.
Graphonomous / Delegatic / body-* dashboards — same reason; they're sections inside either WebHost.Systems (ops) or RuneFort (viz).
Each bundle directory is a manifest + symlinks to source files in the repo. If you update the source, the bundle auto-reflects on next tar. Run
in each bundle dir to refresh.
